findings.failure_scenario: A user sends a message in Chat (Chat.tsx:189) or ChatbotDialog (ChatbotDialog.tsx:193); both render <ChatInput> without onCancel. While the assistant response streams, ChatInput renders the enabled CancelButton; clicking it runs handleSubmit, which reaches onCancel?.() — a no-op because the prop is undefined — and neither caller has an AbortController for the fetch stream. The UI promises cancellation but nothing happens; the user is stuck waiting for the full response.
findings.summary: The CancelButton rendered during loading is inert: no production caller passes onCancel, so clicking Cancel does nothing while the stream continues.

findings.failure_scenario: A keyboard user types a question and presses Enter. Previously the single-line <Input> inside the form triggered implicit submission via onSubmit={handleSubmit}; now Enter inserts a newline and no submission occurs, and the buttons' click default (form submission) is canceled by handleSubmit's preventDefault, so the form's onSubmit never fires at all. Keyboard-only users have no way to send a message — they must click the SendButton with a mouse.
findings.summary: Replacing the single-line Input with a textarea removes Enter-to-send: no keydown handler exists, Enter inserts a newline, and browsers never implicitly submit forms containing textareas.

findings.failure_scenario: A parent renders <ChatInput error={true} /> after a failed send. SendButton receives disabled={isLoading || error} and stays disabled regardless of content; the textarea remains editable, but ChatInput exposes no onChange/onEdit callback for the parent to observe edits and clear the error, so the user can retype the message yet can never resend — the only escape is unmounting the component.
findings.summary: When error is true the send button is permanently disabled with no in-component path to clear the error, dead-ending the input.

findings.failure_scenario: The design system defines --primary-accent: #1ded83 and --danger-default: #c64427 in frontend/packages/ui/src/styles/Dark/variables.css; the hardcoded hover border #459a72 and error border #9c5b5a match neither token. Because they are literals, theme changes (the token files are organized per theme, e.g. Dark/) will not propagate to these states, so hover/error colors permanently diverge from the rest of the UI and from the component's own var()-based styling.
findings.summary: Hardcoded hex/rgba colors (#459a72, #9c5b5a and their glows) bypass the design-token variables used by every other component, and the literals do not match the tokens.

findings.failure_scenario: A parent renders <ChatInput initialMessage='draft A' /> and later re-renders with initialMessage='draft B' (e.g., switching conversations or restoring a draft after an error). useState(initialMessage) keeps 'draft A' and the useEffect([], ...) resize at lines 29-37 does not re-run, so the textarea shows stale text at a stale height.
findings.summary: message state is initialized from initialMessage only once and the mount-only resize effect never re-runs, so later changes to the initialMessage prop are silently ignored.

findings.failure_scenario: If the textarea's min-height in ChatInput.module.css is changed (e.g., to a spacing token or for a larger font size), the setTimeout reset still forces height: '24px' after every send, leaving the empty textarea mis-sized (clipped placeholder or layout jump) with no link between the inline value and the stylesheet.
findings.summary: The post-send height reset hardcodes '24px', duplicating the min-height: 24px value in ChatInput.module.css so the JS and CSS can desync.

findings.failure_scenario: The ui package already re-exports these components at its root (frontend/packages/ui/src/components/index.ts line 9), which is the import path used by the rest of the app. The deep src import works only because package.json has no 'exports' field; adding one (or moving the Tooltip directory) breaks both new buttons while root-export consumers keep working, and it duplicates an existing public API surface for no reason.
findings.summary: Imports Tooltip components from the deep '@liam-hq/ui/src/components/Tooltip' path instead of the package's root export (same in SendButton.tsx line 8).
